column4: Visit note | 2025-08-18 12:00 PM | Dr. Nasrin Sultana, Gastroenterology | Patient: Rezaul Faruque, 26, male. Mr. Faruque presents complaining of cramping belly pain and stools that switch between loose and hard. He mentions this began after a bout of food poisoning in Sylhet. He works as a journalist, eats irregular meals on duty, and denies any fever, blood in stool, or unexplained weight loss. On examination: pain score 5/10, BP 126/70 mmHg, pulse 89 bpm, weight 52 kg. Abdomen is soft with mild tenderness in the left lower quadrant, and bowel sounds are normal. Assessment: Irritable bowel syndrome. Plan: lifestyle and self-care advice only, no new medicine was prescribed at this stage. He was advised to eat regular meals, keep a food diary, and reduce tea, fizzy drinks, and beans. Follow-up in 6 weeks with the food diary.

Visit note | 2025-08-19 10:30 AM | Dr. Zahid Hasan, Gastroenterology | Patient: Hafsa Bepari, 48, female. Mrs. Bepari reports urgent loose stools every morning with little pain, alongside cramping belly pain that is worse with stress. She states this has been worse since starting a high-pressure job in Dhanmondi. She denies vomiting or nocturnal symptoms. On examination: pain score 6/10, BP 127/82 mmHg, pulse 82 bpm, weight 84 kg. Soft abdomen with generalized tenderness, no masses felt. Assessment: Irritable bowel syndrome. Plan: lifestyle and self-care advice only, no new medicine was prescribed at this stage. She was advised to eat regular meals, keep a food diary, and reduce tea, fizzy drinks, and beans. Follow-up in 6 weeks with the food diary.

Visit note | 2025-08-23 11:00 AM | Dr. Rumana Haque, Endocrinology | Patient: Karim Bhuiyan, 40, male. Mr. Bhuiyan states he has been losing weight without trying, has cuts that heal slowly, and is always feeling thirsty. He notes his sugar readings rose during a busy season at work in Badda. He works as a photographer, has a known history of Hypothyroidism, and denies visual changes or chest pain. On examination: fasting glucose 12.6 mmol/L, BP 127/80 mmHg, pulse 69 bpm, weight 66 kg. Foot examination shows intact pulses with normal sensation. Assessment: Type 2 diabetes mellitus. Plan: tests ordered before starting treatment, including HbA1c, fasting glucose, and urine albumin; no new medicine was prescribed today. He was advised to reduce rice portions and sweets, walk briskly 30 minutes five days a week, check fasting sugar twice weekly, and check the feet daily. Follow-up after the test results are ready.

Visit note | 2025-08-24 02:00 PM | Dr. Jannatul Ferdous, Orthopedics | Patient: Nazmul Sikder, 67, male. Mr. Sikder describes stiffness in the morning for a few minutes, a creaking knee, and knee pain on the stairs. He mentions this is worse since standing all day at a shop in Rampura. He works as a shopkeeper, has Essential hypertension, and denies joint redness or locking. On examination: BMI 33.4, BP 143/93 mmHg, pulse 80 bpm, weight 90 kg. Both knees show mild crepitus and restricted flexion without effusion. Assessment: Knee osteoarthritis. Plan: tests ordered before starting treatment: a knee X-ray; no new medicine was prescribed at this visit. He was advised to do thigh-strengthening exercises daily, lose weight, and avoid squatting and sitting cross-legged on the floor. Follow-up after the test results are ready.

Visit note | 2025-08-27 10:30 AM | Dr. Nasrin Sultana, Gastroenterology | Patient: Shamim Karim, 75, male. Mr. Karim complains of burning behind the breastbone after meals, a sour taste in the mouth, and symptoms that are worse when lying down. He notes this began after gaining weight while working from home in Bashundhara. He works as a shopkeeper, has Essential hypertension, and denies difficulty swallowing or unintended weight loss. On examination: BMI 32.4, BP 149/96 mmHg, pulse 85 bpm, weight 83 kg. Abdomen is soft and non-tender. Assessment: Gastro-oesophageal reflux disease. Plan: tests ordered before starting treatment: no tests unless symptoms persist; no new medicine was prescribed today. He was advised to eat smaller meals, avoid oily and spicy food late at night, and raise the head of the bed. Follow-up after the test results are ready.

Visit note | 2025-08-27 10:30 AM | Dr. Zahid Hasan, Gastroenterology | Patient: Ibrahim Sarkar, 65, male. Mr. Sarkar presents with a long-standing dry cough and hoarse voice with little heartburn, burning behind the breastbone after meals, symptoms worse when lying down, and a sour taste in the mouth. He reports it began after gaining weight while working from home in Old Dhaka. He works as a farmer, has Essential hypertension, and denies fever or shortness of breath. On examination: BMI 29.1, BP 149/94 mmHg, pulse 74 bpm, weight 91 kg. Chest is clear and abdomen is soft. Assessment: Gastro-oesophageal reflux disease. Plan: lifestyle and self-care advice only, no new medicine was prescribed at this stage. He was advised to eat smaller meals, avoid oily and spicy food late at night, and raise the head of the bed. Follow-up in 1 month.

Visit note | 2025-08-28 04:00 PM | Dr. Sabrina Chowdhury, Cardiology | Patient: Tamim Siddique, 57, male. Mr. Siddique states he has no symptoms, mentions a father who had a heart attack at 55, and notes high cholesterol found on a routine test in an office health check in Cox's Bazar. He works as a shopkeeper and denies chest pain, palpitations, or dizziness. On examination: LDL cholesterol 4.9 mmol/L, BP 136/72 mmHg, pulse 87 bpm, weight 47 kg. Heart sounds are normal and peripheral pulses are intact. Assessment: Dyslipidaemia. Plan: tests ordered before starting treatment: a fasting lipid profile and liver function tests; no new medicine was prescribed today. He was advised to reduce fried food, red meat, and ghee, walk 30 minutes daily, and aim to lose 3 kg. Follow-up after the test results are ready.

Visit note | 2025-09-01 11:00 AM | Dr. Nazma Begum, Obstetrics and Gynecology | Patient: Nargis Howlader, 33, female. Mrs. Howlader reports irregular periods and extra hair on the face. She noticed weight gain after starting a desk job in Jashore. She works as a schoolteacher and denies pelvic pain, hot flushes, or skin discoloration. On examination: BMI 26.1, BP 112/71 mmHg, pulse 85 bpm, weight 76 kg. Abdomen is soft, no adnexal masses palpable. Assessment: Polycystic ovary syndrome. Plan: tests ordered before starting treatment: a pelvic ultrasound and hormone profile; no new medicine was prescribed at this visit. She was advised to aim for 5% weight loss, exercise 150 minutes a week, and reduce sugary drinks. Follow-up after the test results are ready.

Visit note | 2025-09-01 03:30 PM | Dr. Zahid Hasan, Gastroenterology | Patient: Dipak Bose, 70, male. Mr. Bose describes a sour taste in the mouth and symptoms that are worse when lying down. He notes this became worse since a job change in Gazipur meant late heavy dinners. He works as a tailor and denies difficulty swallowing, chest pressure, or vomiting. On examination: BMI 30.9, BP 130/83 mmHg, pulse 84 bpm, weight 64 kg. Abdomen is soft with no tenderness. Assessment: Gastro-oesophageal reflux disease. Plan: lifestyle and self-care advice only, no new medicine was prescribed at this stage. He was advised to eat smaller meals, avoid oily and spicy food late at night, and raise the head of the bed. Follow-up in 1 month.
